app.name: Anycubic Toolkit
app.tagline: The open-source companion for your Anycubic printer

splash.donate_hint: Anycubic Toolkit is free and open source. Donations keep it alive.

dashboard.subtitle: Here is the current state of your printer at a glance.
dashboard.no_news: No news available. Connect to the internet to load the latest updates.
dashboard.get_started: Drop an AC_LOG.pack in the Log Analyzer to get started.
dashboard.help: This is your home screen — a quick overview of your printer and any news. New here? Start with Log Analysis (drag in a file from your printer), or open Firmware and pick your model. Everything runs on your computer.

log.title: Log Analyzer
log.subtitle: Drop an AC_LOG.pack file — it is unlocked and analyzed locally.
log.privacy: Your logs never leave this computer. Only the password database is downloaded.
log.help: Your Anycubic printer can save a diagnostics file called AC_LOG.pack (export it from the printer’s settings onto a USB stick). Drag that file onto this page — the app unlocks it and reads it to find your printer model, firmware and any errors, then gives a health score. Nothing is uploaded; it all stays on your computer.

errors.title: Error Code Lookup
errors.subtitle: Enter an Anycubic error code to see causes and fixes.
errors.source: Error data is sourced from the Anycubic Wiki.
errors.browse_all: Browse all error codes on the Anycubic Wiki
errors.full_guide: Full troubleshooting steps are on the Anycubic Wiki page for this code.
errors.help: See a number on your printer’s screen when something goes wrong? Type that error code here and the app fetches the explanation straight from the official Anycubic Wiki — what it means and how to fix it.

printer.title: Printer Information
printer.subtitle: Identity of the printer detected from your last log analysis.
printer.no_data: No printer detected yet. Analyze an AC_LOG.pack first.
printer.help: Shows the details detected from your most recent log: model, serial number and firmware version. Analyze a log file first (on the Log Analysis page) and they appear here.

firmware.title: Firmware Center
firmware.subtitle: Installed firmware, available releases and rollback versions.
firmware.installed_unknown: Unknown — analyze a log to detect it
firmware.no_data: No firmware information available. Check your connection and refresh.
firmware.from_official: Listed on the official Anycubic firmware & software page.
firmware.not_in_catalog: No Rinkhals firmware catalog for this model yet — use the official Anycubic page below.
firmware.kobra_x_notice: Rinkhals doesn't support the Kobra X yet — its firmware uses a newer, RSA-signed format that hasn't been cracked open, so there's no verified, checksummed catalog for it. Get firmware from Anycubic's official page below. A community-shared archive also exists, but its files aren't checksum-verified by this app — use it at your own risk.
firmware.catalog_source: Firmware list from the Rinkhals community catalog.
firmware.help: Firmware is the software that runs on your printer. Pick your model (or analyze a log first) and the app lists the available firmware versions with their change notes. Your installed version is marked. Only update if you have a reason to, and read the notes first.

rinkhals.title: Rinkhals
rinkhals.subtitle: Open-source custom firmware for Anycubic Kobra
rinkhals.description: Rinkhals is an open-source custom firmware for Anycubic Kobra printers. It adds Moonraker, Mainsail/Fluidd, an app system and more — while keeping the stock experience. This toolkit uses its public firmware catalog to list downloads for your model.
rinkhals.note: Live printer connection (Moonraker) for Rinkhals-equipped printers is planned.
rinkhals.release_unknown: Could not reach GitHub for the latest release right now.
rinkhals.model_supported: Rinkhals maintains a firmware catalog for your {model}.
rinkhals.model_unsupported: Rinkhals has no firmware catalog for your {model} yet.
rinkhals.help: Rinkhals is an optional open-source custom firmware that adds features (like network control) to Anycubic Kobra printers. This page shows the latest version and links to install guides. You don’t need it to use this app — it’s for tinkerers who want more control.

connect.title: Connect Printers
connect.subtitle: Live status for all your printers, over Moonraker or Anycubic LAN mode
connect.description: Add each printer's IP address below. The app connects locally to every one — via Moonraker if it runs Rinkhals, or via Anycubic LAN mode on stock firmware (e.g. Kobra X; enable LAN mode in the printer settings). Nothing goes through any cloud.
connect.already_added: That printer is already in your list.
connect.empty: No printers added yet — enter an IP address above to add your first one.
connect.import_invalid: That file doesn't look like a printer list.
connect.monitor: Keep monitoring all printers in the background (history, notifications, Home Assistant)
connect.offline: Could not reach the printer. Check the IP and that Rinkhals/Moonraker is running.
connect.help: Your printer can be reached over your home network in two ways. If it runs the Rinkhals custom firmware, the app talks to Moonraker. If it runs the original firmware (like the Kobra X), enable LAN mode in the printer's settings and the app connects directly — no account or cloud needed. Add each printer's IP address below (find it in your router or the printer's network menu) — the app monitors all of them at once. The first LAN-mode connection pairs with each printer once and remembers it.
connect.mode_lan: Connected via Anycubic LAN mode (stock firmware)
connect.lan_missing_mqtt: LAN mode found, but the MQTT component (paho-mqtt) is missing from this build.
connect.cloud_hint_token: A login token from Anycubic Slicer Next was found on this computer. Fetch your printers’ status via the cloud below.
connect.cloud_hint_no_token: No login token found. Log in to Anycubic Slicer Next once on this computer, or paste your access token below.
connect.cloud_no_printers: No printers found on this account.

health.title: Printer Health
health.subtitle: Component scores computed from your last log analysis.
health.no_data: No health data yet. Analyze an AC_LOG.pack first.
health.help: A simple score from 0 to 100 for your printer and its main parts (extruder, bed, motors and so on), based on your last analyzed log. Low scores point you to what may need attention.

report.title: Support Report
report.subtitle: Bundle your analysis into a report you can attach to a support ticket.
report.includes: The report includes printer identity, firmware, health scores, errors and warnings from the last analysis, plus Toolkit version and OS details. Log files themselves are not included.
report.no_data: Analyze an AC_LOG.pack first to generate a report.
report.privacy: credentials, Wi-Fi, MAC and serial are masked for safe sharing
report.help: Creates a tidy text summary of your analysis that you can paste into a support ticket or forum post. Sensitive details like your Wi-Fi and serial number are masked automatically, so it’s safe to share.

resources.title: Resources & Tools
resources.subtitle: Model libraries, AI generators, slicers and Anycubic links
resources.libraries_note: Where to find printable models. MakerWorld hosts Bambu Lab models, but their .3mf files print fine on Anycubic after a quick pass through Anycubic Slicer Next.
resources.ai_note: Turn text or images into 3D models. Meshy is the most print-focused; the others are strong alternatives.
resources.slicers_note: Anycubic Slicer Next (OrcaSlicer-based) is official for the Kobra series. OrcaSlicer is the best alternative; Cura and PrusaSlicer also work with the right profile.
resources.anycubic_note: Official Anycubic EU store, firmware/software and wiki.
resources.fleet_note: Running many printers at once? This toolkit stays focused on one machine at a time — for real fleet dispatch and job queuing, try a dedicated tool:
resources.help: Handy links for your printer: where to download models, AI tools that turn text or images into 3D models, slicer software (which converts a model into a file your printer can print), and official Anycubic pages. Everything opens in your web browser.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Language, appearance, updates and folders.
settings.auto_update: Check for updates automatically on start
settings.help: Change the app’s language and light/dark theme, choose where downloads are saved, and set your printer and connection preferences here.
settings.cloud_note: Optional: check your printers via your Anycubic account when you are away from your home network. Uses an unofficial API that Anycubic may change at any time. Only status is read — never remote control. The login token is stored locally on this computer and is cleared when you turn this off.
settings.notify_toggle: Notify me when a print finishes or fails
settings.notify_note: Sends a message via ntfy (free phone app, no account), a Discord webhook or any webhook URL. Requires background monitoring on the Connect page.
settings.notify_target_placeholder: ntfy topic name or webhook URL
settings.ha_toggle: Publish printer status to Home Assistant (MQTT)
settings.ha_note: Publishes your printer as sensors in Home Assistant via MQTT Discovery — state, progress, temperatures, layer and time remaining appear automatically as a device. Enter your MQTT broker (usually the Mosquitto add-on). Requires background monitoring on the Connect page.
settings.ha_test_missing: MQTT component (paho-mqtt) missing from this build.

about.title: About
about.description: Anycubic Toolkit is a free, open-source desktop utility for Anycubic 3D printer owners: log analysis, error lookup, firmware tracking, health monitoring and a plugin system.
about.made_with: Built with Python and Qt. Not affiliated with Anycubic.
about.help: Version details, credits and links for the app — including where to get help and how to support the project.

updates.latest: You are running the latest version ({version}).

passwords.none: No password database is available yet. Connect to the internet so it can be downloaded; log analysis needs it to unlock the archive.
passwords.stale: The password database is {days} days old. Connect to the internet to refresh it.

history.title: Print History
history.subtitle: Prints recorded while monitoring is active
history.stats: {total} prints  •  {finished} finished, {failed} failed ({rate}% success)  •  total print time {time}
history.empty: No prints recorded yet. Connect to your printer and enable background monitoring on the Connect page — finished and failed prints will appear here.
history.help: While background monitoring is on (Connect page), every print the app sees is saved here on your computer: file name, result, duration and date. Use it to spot failure patterns and keep track of printing hours for maintenance. Clearing removes the local records only.
